sections.html:
Roanoke County surrounds two independent cities, Roanoke and Salem. Both sit within its borders yet answer to their own city governments. Vinton is the lone incorporated town in the county proper. The courthouse remains in Salem, the county seat, from the time Salem turned independent in 1968, while the county's administrative offices relocated to the Cave Spring area. Check which building you are headed to before you go for an appointment or a form.

A Roanoke or Salem mailing address on a county parcel is common, and it can mislead you about who taxes the house. Roanoke County, Roanoke, Salem and Vinton each have separate rates and offices. Pin down which one bills your parcel before you appeal, pay or request a payoff. The bill itself and the county's parcel records will tell you.

  • Named communities with their own identity include Cave Spring, Glenvar and Hollins.
  • Unincorporated areas include Back Creek, Bent Mountain, Bonsack, Catawba, Clearbrook, Hanging Rock, Masons Cove, Mount Pleasant, Oak Grove, Penn Forest and Poages Mill.
  • Vinton runs under its own council and manager.

sections.h2: What sellers find in the county
sections.html:
Population stood at 96,929 in 2020, concentrated in suburbs around Roanoke and Salem, with rural, mountainous ground to the north, west and south. Of 42,147 housing units, 5.6 percent sat vacant, and three quarters of occupied units, 75.5 percent, were lived in by their owners. Inherited family houses and downsizing moves are therefore typical reasons to sell.

Interstate 81 and Interstate 581 pass through, along with the Blue Ridge Parkway and a slice of the Jefferson National Forest. Out in the rural parts, a parcel may rely on a private road, a well or a septic system. On Virginia's seller disclosure form the owner makes no statement about wastewater systems, lot lines, easements or special flood hazard areas, and buyers are told to look into them. Having a recent survey, a septic pumping record and a driveway maintenance agreement on hand can rescue a deal.

Own a big parcel? The real estate valuation office can say whether a special land-use program covers it. Changing how land is used can bring additional taxes, and the disclosure form starting January 1, 2027 adds a line about roll-back taxes on land taxed by its use.

Begin informally by asking the county's real estate valuation office to walk you through the value. Ask the office for its phone number and schedule. Virginia law then offers a hearing before the Board of Equalization.

At the hearing the proof is on you. The assessor starts out presumed right. Your evidence must outweigh that presumption by showing the value is higher than fair market value, is not uniform with similar property, or was not set using accepted appraisal practice. Note the board is free to raise a figure as well as cut it, in the name of an even tax burden.

  • Sales that closed up to the December 31 before the effective date count, provided you submit them by the locality's cutoff.
  • Studies published after that December 31 are left out.
  • Owners of residential property with fewer than four units can request the assessor's records in writing and are entitled to them within 15 days.

Virginia Code 58.1-3379 is the controlling statute. Because deadlines change with the locality and the year, get this year's cutoff from the county before you start gathering evidence.

These routes fix different problems. A correction request is sent to the commissioner of the revenue or a similar officer, while an appeal asks the board for a fresh valuation. Virginia Code 58.1-3980 limits corrections on real estate to mistakes made by the assessing office, or factual errors by others during a general reassessment.

You have until the later of three years after the tax year ends or one year after the assessment. Typical mistakes include wrong square footage, a finished basement that was never built, or a parcel entered twice. Such errors can be fixed without any debate over market value.

Tax on real estate holds the top lien position, and it remains on the property until the tax office is paid. Sale proceeds must go first to unpaid tax, penalties and interest included, handled by the closing agent. The treasurer lifts the lien once payment arrives.

Virginia Code 58.1-3340 leaves the year's split to the contract, so the purchase agreement needs to say who owes which share. A partial sale of a tract sends proceeds toward the whole tract's taxes in proportion to price, and a low price may prompt the assessing office to ask for an appraisal.

Separately, Virginia Code 58.1-802 sets a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of price. The seller owes it unless the contract says differently, and it is divided between the state and the locality.

A cash sale keeps things simple when taxes are behind. The title company takes the tax balance out of your proceeds, sends it to the treasurer and pays you the rest.

sections.h2: What to bring to the valuation office
sections.html: Walk in prepared. Take your tax bill or parcel number, the address as it appears on the deed, and photographs of anything the record gets wrong. If you are questioning the value, add sales of comparable homes and any recent appraisal or repair estimate. If you are claiming a factual error, write down exactly what the record says and what is true, for example the number of finished rooms. Ask how the office wants the request submitted and when it expects to answer. Keep a copy of everything you hand over, along with the name of the person who took it, so you can follow up if the office is slow to reply.

Pin down the billing locality first. Then get a written payoff from the treasurer. Compare the assessor's record of your house with reality: square footage, finished space and condition notes. If you find a factual error, a correction request may be the faster fix. If the value seems high compared with recent sales, collect those sales before the board deadline. For a large or rural parcel, line up the survey, the septic record and any road agreement so buyers can see them early.

faqs.q: Is Salem part of Roanoke County?
faqs.a: No. It is an independent city located within the county's borders. Salem hosts the courthouse as county seat, but the county's offices are in the Cave Spring area.

faqs.q: Who has the burden of proof at a Roanoke County Board of Equalization hearing?
faqs.a: The taxpayer. Virginia Code 58.1-3379 presumes the assessor's value is right, so you need to show it exceeds fair market value or lacks uniformity.

faqs.q: Can I fix a factual error on my assessment after the appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Possibly. A correction request is open for three years after the tax year ends or one year after the assessment, whichever is later, and covers only errors by the assessing office or in a general reassessment.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay the real estate tax lien at closing?
faqs.a: Neither, directly. Unpaid tax is paid out of the proceeds, which means the seller's share reduces the seller's check. The contract splits the current year.

faqs.q: What is the Virginia grantor's tax on a Roanoke County sale?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for every $500 of price. Sellers pay it unless the buyer agrees to, and the clerk collects it at recording.
